lists.description: Jonathan Hickman's rebuilt Ultimate line in publication-adjacent reading order, from Ultimate Invasion (2023) through Ultimate Impact: Reborn.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: The New Ultimate Universe: Collected Editions
lists.description: The same line read the way it is collected, one section per trade paperback, for readers who buy the books rather than the single issues. Each section is a volume you can buy, and it tracks its own progress. Reading is shared with the issue-by-issue order, so an issue ticked in one is ticked in the other. The volume line-up follows Comic Book Herald's collected-edition guide and is not derived from Marvel metadata, which carries no collection records for this era. Six issues Marvel has not collected are left out: the 2024 Free Comic Book Day issue and the five-part Ultimate Impact: Reborn.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: House of M
lists.description: Wanda Maximoff rewrites the world in Marvel's 2005 event, in publication order: the eight-issue main series, its branded tie-in mini-series, and the Decimation epilogue. Assembled from Marvel series metadata, so it covers the series Marvel branded with the event name and not the House of M chapters published in unbranded ongoing titles such as Wolverine #33-35.

lists.name: X-Men: Silver Age to Claremont
lists.description: The X-Men from their 1963 debut to the year after the Mutant Massacre, in one order: the Lee and Kirby run, Giant-Size X-Men and the Claremont and Cockrum relaunch, the Phoenix, Dark Phoenix and Brood sagas, Days of Future Past, God Loves Man Kills, and the arrival of the New Mutants and X-Factor. Compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guides, read as a reference and re-expressed here, so the order is not derived from Marvel metadata and cannot be checked against it. The Mutant Massacre is read in the crossover's own interleaved order. X-Men #67-93 are left out because all 27 are reprints of issues this order already carries and Marvel holds no metadata for the reprint years. The outline ran out partway through X-Factor's second year, so this stops at X-Factor #23 and reaches neither Fall of the Mutants nor Inferno.
lists.variant: The spine, without the optional reading
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: X-Men: Silver Age to Claremont, with the optional reading
lists.description: The same order as the spine beside it, plus the two sections the outline marked optional. Compiled by hand from the same reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guides. The Silver Age add-ons are the guest appearances that carried the X-Men through the years their own title was running reprints, scattered across Amazing Adventures, Spider-Man, the Hulk, the Avengers, Captain America, the Defenders and Giant-Size Fantastic Four. The modern retellings revisit the same years from the outside: The Hidden Years, Grand Design, Season One and the whole of First Class. X-Men Annual #1 and #2 are listed without a link, because Marvel's metadata carries that series only from #3.
lists.variant: With the optional add-ons and retellings
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: The Best of Captain America
lists.description: A best-of path through Captain America on Marvel Unlimited, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to the same. Ed Brubaker's run comes first and whole, from the Winter Soldier's return through the death of Steve Rogers, Reborn, Rebirth and the restored numbering, followed by Man Out of Time and the Life of Bucky Barnes. It then goes back for the Silver and Bronze Age chapters the guide picks out: the Red Skull and the Cosmic Cube in Tales of Suspense, the Life and Times of the Red Skull, Mark Gruenwald's The Captain, and issue #250 as a bonus. The sections are the guide's and are kept in its order rather than sorted by publication date.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: There is Only Doom
lists.description: A primer on Doctor Doom, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to the best Doom comics. It opens with the origin, in Fantastic Four #5, the second Fantastic Four annual and the Ultimate retelling, then Books of Doom and the story of Werner von Doom. From there it follows Doom as monarch, rival and thief of power: the long Fantastic Four sieges, Doomquest in Iron Man, the Silver Surfer and the Power Cosmic, Secret Wars in 1984 and again in 2015, the Infinity Gauntlet, and his turn as a hero in Infamous Iron Man. The sections are the guide's and are kept in its order.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Best of Spider-Man
lists.description: A best-of path through Peter Parker's Spider-Man, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to the same. It runs from Amazing Fantasy #15 and the Lee and Ditko years through the Lee and Romita chapters, Roger Stern's Hobgoblin mystery, the death of Jean DeWolff, Kraven's Last Hunt read across all three titles in publication order, the decline of Harry Osborn, Straczynski's Coming Home, the Gauntlet and Grim Hunt, Dying Wish into Superior Spider-Man, and Life Story. The sections are the guide's and are kept in its order rather than sorted by publication date.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Best of Thor
lists.description: A best-of path through Thor, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to the same. It starts in Journey into Mystery with the Absorbing Man and the issue where the title becomes Thor, then Kirby's cosmic run with Ego, the High Evolutionary and Mangog, Firelord, the Celestial Saga, and Walt Simonson's Surtur Saga with Beta Ray Bill and Skurge's last stand. It then covers the final Ragnarok, Asgard over Nebraska, Jason Aaron's God Butcher and Malekith stories, Jane Foster's run as Thor, and the War of the Realms. The sections are the guide's and are kept in its order.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Best of the Scarlet Witch
lists.description: A best-of path through Wanda Maximoff, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to the same. It opens with her origin one-shot and the issue where she meets Agatha Harkness, then the Chthon possession on Wundagore Mountain, both Vision and the Scarlet Witch limited series, and her inner world in Avengers. It carries on through the Children's Crusade, Wanda under the Apocalypse Twins in Ragnarok Now, her 2015 solo series, her break with Wonder Man, Quicksilver's side of their bond, and No Road Home. The sections are the guide's and are kept in its order.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Essential Avengers
lists.description: Ten runs out of the first 285 issues of Avengers, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. It takes the team from its assembly and the return of Captain America through the arrival of the Vision, the Kree and Skrull War, the Bride of Ultron, the Korvac Saga, the nights of Wundagore, Heart of Stone, the legacy of Thanos, Under Siege and the assault on Olympus. The gaps between sections are the outline's own: this is a selection rather than a continuous read.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Avengers Disassembled
lists.description: The 2004 story that pulls the Avengers apart, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. It is four issues of Brian Michael Bendis at the end of the 1998 series plus the one-shot that closes it out, and it is the shortest order in this catalog on purpose. It ends the Busiek, Perez and Johns era and sets up everything the modern Avengers books do next.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Civil War: An Avengers Reading List
lists.description: The Avengers path through Civil War and out the other side, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. It pairs the seven-issue event with the New Avengers issues that run alongside it, the Young Avengers and Runaways tie-in, and Warren Ellis and Mike Deodato's Thunderbolts, which is not an Avengers title but is what makes Dark Avengers make sense later. It then follows the split into Mighty Avengers, the Initiative, Avengers/Invaders and the Illuminati.
lists.variant: The Avengers path, through the war and past it
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Dark Reign: An Avengers Reading List
lists.description: The Avengers path through Dark Reign, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. Norman Osborn runs his own Avengers, the Initiative and the real team go underground, and the Utopia crossover interrupts Dark Avengers partway through, which is why the run is read with a gap and picked up again later. It closes with Dark Reign: Young Avengers and the Children's Crusade.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Heroic Age: An Avengers Reading List
lists.description: The Avengers titles of 2010 to 2012 read together, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. Avengers, New Avengers and Secret Avengers alternate volume by volume from the Heroic Age launch through Fear Itself and on to the edge of Avengers vs X-Men, with Avengers Prime as the prologue. Where two of the outline's volumes share an issue at the boundary, it is read once, in the earlier one.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: All-New, All-Different Avengers
lists.description: The Avengers line after Secret Wars, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. Rage of Ultron opens it, then the All-New, All-Different team, Uncanny Avengers, the A.I.M. New Avengers and A-Force, through the Standoff and Civil War II eras and into Secret Empire. It also carries the smaller books of the period, Great Lakes Avengers, Occupy Avengers and U.S.Avengers, in the order the outline gives them.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Marvel Fresh Start Avengers
lists.description: Jason Aaron's Avengers and the books around it, compiled by hand from a reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guide to Avengers trade collections. The Final Host assembles the team, Wakanda Forever runs across three one-shots and an annual, and the West Coast Avengers and Savage Avengers run alongside the main title through the World Tour, the War of the Vampires and No Road Home. The gaps in the main series are the outline's own.

paths.description: The shared Avengers story from the Silver Age through to the Fresh Start era, as a sequence of stops. Each stop is a story you can read at whichever depth you prefer; no two stops share an issue, so nothing is read twice.
